framework/read_skill-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'read_skill' is reserved when ≥1 Skill is registered. Rename your custom 'read_skill' tool or unregister it.

framework/skip_step-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'skip_step' is reserved when any skill declares `steps` — the framework auto-attaches the procedure-integrity tool under that name, and a same-named tool would silently take over the model's recorded skips. Rename your tool.

framework/run_overview-vs-static.because: AgentBuilder.selfExplain: tool name 'run_overview' is reserved by .selfExplain() (inline mode). The tools slot dedupes by name (first wins), so your tool would silently shadow the trace tool. Rename it, or reserved names: run_overview, find_context_errors, find_in_trace, trace_node, trace_slice, backtrack, who_wrote, get_value, inspect_tool_call, inspect_tool_run, read_narrative.

framework/present-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'present' is reserved when an artifact store is attached — the framework auto-attaches the hand-to-the-screen tool under that name, and a same-named tool would silently take over the model's presentations. Rename your tool, or drop the `artifacts` store.

framework/skip_step-vs-skill-active.because: Agent: tool name 'skip_step' is reserved when any skill declares `steps` — the framework auto-attaches the procedure-integrity tool under that name, and a same-named tool would silently take over the model's recorded skips. Rename your tool.

collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND an ACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, activated)
collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.cause: the wire carried 'mcp's contract and 'skill-active's implementation answered, inside epoch 2
collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.tolerated: The documented shadow seam. The wire merge is [static, provider, skill, step] first-occurrence-wins and an autoActivate skill's tools are deliberately kept out of the static registry, so the PROVIDER's schema is what the model reads; lookupTool checks registryByName first, where every skill tool lives and no provider tool does, so the SKILL's execute is what runs. Reported rather than refused because there is no build-time moment at which the pair is knowable: the provider's list is resolved per iteration and the skill has to be active. Pinned by test/toolShadowing.test.ts and epoch-laws 1(g).

collision/mcp-then-skill-inactive::share.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND an INACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, never activated)
collision/mcp-then-skill-inactive::share.cause: the wire carried 'mcp's contract and 'skill-inactive's implementation answered, inside epoch 1
collision/mcp-then-skill-inactive::share.tolerated: ROUND 3, and a genuine defect. Identical mechanism to the active-skill shadow above, with the event missing: reportShadowedTools walks activeInjections, but registryByName holds EVERY skill tool — an autoActivate skill's included, whether or not it is active — and lookupTool reads that map first. So the model reads a provider's contract, an INACTIVE skill's implementation answers, and nothing is on the record. Not fixed here: widening the report's input from the active set to the dispatch map emits events in runs that emit none today, which is a behaviour change and gets its own decision.

collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND a skill’s `tools:[]` with tools always visible (no `autoActivate`)
collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.cause: 'mcp' registered 'shared_tool' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; nothing was reported
collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.tolerated: The mirror of the shadow seam, and unreported. The merge is first-occurrence-wins with the static registry list first, and lookupTool reads registryByName before the provider cache — so a provider tool whose name a registry-list holder already owns loses the wire AND dispatch, and is dead in both directions. reportShadowedTools cannot see it: it fires only when a provider schema SURVIVED the merge. The model is never misled here (it reads one contract and calls that same implementation), so this is the author's problem rather than the model's — but it is silent, and the build cannot refuse it because the provider's list is per-iteration. Reporting it is a behaviour change.

collision/mcp-then-step-skill::shared_to.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND a STEPPED skill’s step-1 tool, with the tenure open
collision/mcp-then-step-skill::shared_to.cause: the event says the model read the provider's schema; the wire carried 'step-skill' (skill)
collision/mcp-then-step-skill::shared_to.tolerated: ROUND 3, and a genuine defect. reportShadowedTools hard-codes schemaFrom:'provider', but an ALWAYS-VISIBLE skill's tools ride the STATIC registry list, which merges first — so the SKILL's description is what the model read and the provider's schema was deduped away. In this configuration there is no identity divergence at all (contract and implementation are both the skill's); the only wrong thing in the epoch is the report, which sends an operator to the wrong file. Not fixed here: deriving the winner from the merged list instead of asserting it changes the payload, which is a behaviour change.

collision/step-skill-then-mcp::shared_to.tolerated: ROUND 3, and a genuine defect. reportShadowedTools hard-codes schemaFrom:'provider', but an ALWAYS-VISIBLE skill's tools ride the STATIC registry list, which merges first — so the SKILL's description is what the model read and the provider's schema was deduped away. In this configuration there is no identity divergence at all (contract and implementation are both the skill's); the only wrong thing in the epoch is the report, which sends an operator to the wrong file. Not fixed here: deriving the winner from the merged list instead of asserting it changes the payload, which is a behaviour change.

collision/step-skill-then-provider::shar.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by a STEPPED skill’s step-1 tool, with the tenure open AND a `ToolProvider` (`staticTools`)
collision/step-skill-then-provider::shar.cause: 'provider' registered 'shared_tool' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; the shadow report for this name describes a different pair
collision/step-skill-then-provider::shar.tolerated: The mirror of the shadow seam, and unreported. The merge is first-occurrence-wins with the static registry list first, and lookupTool reads registryByName before the provider cache — so a provider tool whose name a registry-list holder already owns loses the wire AND dispatch, and is dead in both directions. reportShadowedTools cannot see it: it fires only when a provider schema SURVIVED the merge. The model is never misled here (it reads one contract and calls that same implementation), so this is the author's problem rather than the model's — but it is silent, and the build cannot refuse it because the provider's list is per-iteration. Reporting it is a behaviour change. Worse here: an event about this very name DOES fire, describing the step-skill/provider pair, so an operator reading it concludes the provider's schema reached the wire. It did not.

cross-epoch/dynamic-provider-withdraws::.configuration: a `ToolProvider` whose `list(ctx)` serves the tool on iteration 1 only
cross-epoch/dynamic-provider-withdraws::.cause: offered in an earlier epoch and unroutable in epoch 2: the implementation is resolved from this epoch's provider list, so withdrawing the offer withdrew dispatch with it
cross-epoch/dynamic-provider-withdraws::.tolerated: Seed 1, and true by construction rather than by defect. A provider tool's implementation is resolved from providerToolCache.current, which the Tools slot OVERWRITES with this iteration's provider.list(ctx) — so withdrawing the offer withdraws dispatch with it. Same-epoch offer still implies same-epoch dispatch; only the cross-epoch half fails, and making it hold would mean retaining every tool a provider ever served, an un-revocable registry that defeats the point of a dynamic provider. What is owed is a sentence the model can read when it names one, not a wider cache — a behaviour change with its own decision.

framework/present-vs-provider::present::.configuration: the framework's `present` against a `ToolProvider` (`staticTools`), artifact store attached
framework/present-vs-provider::present::.cause: 'provider' registered 'present' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; nothing was reported
framework/present-vs-provider::present::.tolerated: Deliberate in direction, silent in execution. The framework reserves this name the moment it attaches its own tool under it, and refuses a static .tool() or a skill tool that holds it — but the reservation never runs against a ToolProvider, whose list is resolved per iteration and is not visible at build. So the provider's tool loses the wire and dispatch and simply never runs. Tolerated because the framework's tool is the one the model should get; not fixed because saying so at runtime is a new event, and a behaviour change.

framework/read_skill-vs-skill-active::re.configuration: the framework's `read_skill` against an ACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, activated)
framework/read_skill-vs-skill-active::re.cause: 'skill-active' registered 'read_skill' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; nothing was reported
framework/read_skill-vs-skill-active::re.tolerated: A genuine gap, and an inconsistency between the three auto-attached names. A skill tool called 'read_skill' under .toolsFromActiveSkill() is neither refused nor reachable: validateToolNameUniqueness reserves 'read_skill' against the STATIC registry only, and buildToolRegistry adds an autoActivate skill's tools to registryByName only when the name is free — 'read_skill' is not. 'present' and 'skip_step' refuse this exact shape at build. Closing the gap is a new build-time throw, so it is a behaviour change with its own decision.

framework/run_overview-vs-provider::run_.cause: 'framework' registered 'run_overview' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; nothing was reported
framework/run_overview-vs-provider::run_.tolerated: A genuine gap, the same one seen from the other side. .selfExplain() reserves its trace-tool names against this.registry — the static .tool() list — and against nothing else, so a consumer ToolProvider serving 'run_overview' wins both the wire and dispatch and the framework's own trace tool is unreachable. The model is not misled (one contract, that same implementation), but .selfExplain() silently does not self-explain. Widening the reservation is a new build-time throw, and a behaviour change.

framework/run_overview-vs-skill-active::.configuration: `.selfExplain()`'s `run_overview` against an ACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, activated), self-explain activated
framework/run_overview-vs-skill-active::.cause: the wire carried 'framework's contract and 'skill-active's implementation answered, inside epoch 3
framework/run_overview-vs-skill-active::.tolerated: The shadow seam again, with the framework's own trace pack playing the provider: .selfExplain() serves run_overview through skillScopedTools, so its schema wins the wire while an autoActivate skill tool of the same name wins registryByName and answers. Accurately reported (schemaFrom=provider, dispatchTo=skill), which is why it is tolerated on the same terms as the seam itself — and it also shows that .selfExplain()'s reservation, which reads only the static registry, does not cover a skill's tools:[].

framework/skip_step-vs-provider::skip_st.configuration: the framework's `skip_step` against a `ToolProvider` (`staticTools`), tenure open
framework/skip_step-vs-provider::skip_st.cause: the wire carried 'provider's contract and 'framework's implementation answered, inside epoch 2
framework/skip_step-vs-provider::skip_st.tolerated: ROUND 3, and a genuine defect. 'skip_step' is reserved at build against static .tool() tools and skill tools, but a ToolProvider resolves per iteration and is invisible at build; its schema then merges ahead of stepSchemas, so the model reads the provider's contract and the framework's skip_step answers — the procedure advances on a call the model believed was somebody else's tool, with nothing reported. Not fixed here: refusing at compose, or reporting, changes behaviour and gets its own decision.
